{{Short description|Theorem in mathematical logic}}
In [[mathematical logic]], '''Lindström's theorem''' (named after Swedish logician [[Per Lindström]], who published it in 1969) states that [[first-order logic]] is the ''[[Strength (mathematical logic)|strongest logic]]''<ref>In the sense of [[Heinz-Dieter Ebbinghaus]] ''Extended logics: the general framework'' in [[Jon Barwise|K. J. Barwise]] and [[Solomon Feferman|S. Feferman]], editors, ''Model-theoretic logics'', 1985 {{isbn|0-387-90936-2}} page 43</ref> (satisfying certain conditions, e.g. [[closure (mathematics)|closure]] under [[negation|classical negation]]) having both the [[compactness theorem|(countable) compactness property]] and the [[Löwenheim–Skolem theorem|(downward) Löwenheim–Skolem property]].<ref>''A companion to philosophical logic'' by Dale Jacquette 2005 {{isbn|1-4051-4575-7}} page 329</ref>

Lindström's theorem is perhaps the best known result of what later became known as [[abstract model theory]],<ref name="ChangKeisler1990">{{cite book|author1=[[Chen Chung Chang]]|author2=[[H. Jerome Keisler]]|title=Model theory|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uiHq0EmaFp0C&pg=PA127|year=1990|publisher=Elsevier|isbn=978-0-444-88054-3|page=127}}</ref> the basic notion of which is an [[abstract logic]];<ref name="Béziau2005">{{cite book|author=[[Jean-Yves Béziau]]|title=Logica universalis: towards a general theory of logic|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kxe-cANrsysC&pg=PA20|year=2005|publisher=Birkhäuser|isbn=978-3-7643-7259-0|page=20}}</ref> the more general notion of an [[Institution (computer science)|institution]] was later introduced, which advances from a [[set theory|set-theoretical]] notion of model to a [[category theory|category]]-theoretical one.<ref name="Gabbay1994">{{cite book|editor=[[Dov M. Gabbay]]|title=What is a logical system?|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XqCu4XjHrIQC&pg=PA380|year=1994|publisher=Clarendon Press|isbn=978-0-19-853859-2|page=380}}</ref> Lindström had previously obtained a similar result in studying first-order logics extended with [[Lindström quantifier]]s.<ref>[[Jouko Väänänen]], [https://web.archive.org/web/20150326223650/http://www.math.helsinki.fi/logic/opetus/lt/lindstrom_theorem1.pdf Lindström's Theorem]</ref>

Lindström's theorem has been extended to various other systems of logic, in particular [[modal logic]]s by [[Johan van Benthem (logician)|Johan van Benthem]] and [[Sebastian Enqvist]].
